requests.need: Runtime symbolic/text labels for calendar names
requests.why: The canonical result contains cutlet/month names; compile-time Marak names are not runtime data and Core strings are absent.
requests.core_repair: Numeric codes alone would change the externally stated result unless a separate normative name mapping remains outside the program.
requests.anti_imitation: The need is symbolic named output explicitly demanded by the source, not a generic wish for strings.

requests.why: The year sequence crosses year zero and continues to years before it; Core Values are naturals.
source_examples: אחר שנה אחת תבוא שנת אין
requests.core_repair: Sign+magnitude can be encoded in several naturals but is a material source/result rewrite.
requests.anti_imitation: The need comes from the calendar's explicit negative-year numbering, not from assuming an Integer type.

requests.need: Finite ordered runtime collections or equivalent general data relation
requests.why: The algorithm constructs, orders, selects, and traverses runtime collections of candidates, books, permutations, and weavings.
requests.core_repair: Gödel-style numeric encodings are computable but would cease to be ordinary/local Megillah repair.
requests.anti_imitation: No array/list implementation is prescribed; only source-visible ordered finite collection behavior is requested.

requests.why: The Megillah repeatedly branches/orders by רב/ימעט; Core freezes equality/zero but no general numeric order proposition.
requests.core_repair: Possible encodings are non-local and awkward under natural-subtraction domain failure; they obscure rather than locally repair the source.
requests.anti_imitation: The request is the explicit Biblical relation רב/מעט, not a symbolic > or < operator.

requests.need: Productive direct Biblical numeral grammar beyond 9999
requests.why: A-NUM-001 explicitly leaves >9999 as future full-language/Megillah compatibility work.
source_examples: large fixed constants in the sauce/calendar rules
requests.core_repair: Values can be computed from smaller literals, but systematically replacing written numerals would be large and historically distortive.
requests.anti_imitation: This extends Biblical numeral language, not machine-literal syntax.

requests.need: General exact counted recurrence N פעמים for arbitrary admitted natural N
requests.why: The source uses natural counted-repetition wording with counts far beyond the small individually audited Core forms, including 125 and 127.
requests.core_repair: Named recursion can encode the computation, but replacing every ordinary N פעמים occurrence by explicit counters/recursion is non-local.
requests.anti_imitation: The source already says N פעמים in Biblical Hebrew; this is not a request for a conventional for-loop.

requests.need: Explicit external input binding for the two day values
requests.why: The Megillah is parameterized by יום המעשה and היום אשר עליו תשאל, but a Core executable has no source-level external input association.
source_examples: לשני קרא היום אשר עליו תשאל
requests.core_repair: A fixed-query program can hard-code/initialize two places, but that is not the reusable two-input algorithm described by the source.
requests.anti_imitation: No stdin/argv convention is assumed; the request is only an explicit language/host boundary for two source-described input values.
